clue.text: Obstructed hospital electrical unit-damn!

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
the ampere is the SI unit of electric current
the oath is printed politely as 'd—', so damn gives just D

explanation.surface: Someone held up by a faulty piece of hospital electrical kit swears in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'damn!' is not just colour: an old printing habit shows the oath as 'd—', so it supplies D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hampered is to be impeded or held back, a direct synonym of obstructed.

clue.text: Make undue claim for topless English spa ?

indicators.note: topless means the top letter is lost from the spa's name

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A request for a bare-chested English spa resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter (H) from HARROGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize something without justification.

clue.text: Have excess weight before open trade adjustment

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: adjustment means rearranging, so the letters of open trade are reworked

explanation.surface: Being overweight follows a change to a trading arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' rearranges OPENTRADE into PONDERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To preponderate is literally to weigh more, so to outweigh or have excess weight.

clue.text: Rare slip corrected ("tit" for "tat")

indicators.note: correcting a slip means changing the letters around, so rare slip is rearranged

explanation.surface: A typing slip swapped one word for another, tit printed for tat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges RARESLIP; the bracket looks like the slip itself but is the phrase tit for tat, retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means paying back like with like, which is retaliation in kind.

clue.text: Compensation needed as mother is getting old

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
ages means grows older

explanation.surface: A claim made because an elderly mother needs care.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are money awarded by a court to make good a loss or injury.

clue.text: Arouses fury in France

definitions.meaning: the name of a city in the Loire region of France

explanation.walkthrough: The town Angers is pronounced the French way but spelt like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means makes furious, and Angers is a city in western France on the Maine river.

clue.text: We rise to support Sergeant-Major Bird

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant-major

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so we is turned round

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand up in support of their sergeant-major.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns WE to EW; 'to support' puts it below SM.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, the male strikingly white.

clue.text: Got out but continued to bat?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman who knocks the ball onto his own stumps is out in this way

explanation.walkthrough: The cricket dismissal, where the ball comes off the bat into the stumps, also reads as carried on playing.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term for being bowled off one's own bat, and the everyday phrase for keeping going.

clue.text: Jack with a girl at fifty? That's unusual

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor
Norma is a girl's name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A sailor taking up with a woman at the age of fifty raises eyebrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' and 'at' just link the sailor, the girl and the number; 'fifty' looks like an age but is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abnormal departs from the norm, which is what 'that's unusual' remarks on.

clue.text: Fish not on menu, do I hear?

indicators.note: the question asks whether the word is being pronounced, signalling a sound-alike in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: a dish no longer available is 'off' the menu

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the fish has been taken off the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'off' said in a drawl ('orf') sounds like ORFE; 'Fish' sits in the surface as food but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often kept golden in ornamental ponds.

clue.text: Pool investment re method.. laid down by BR

parts.note: a perm (permutation) is a combination entry on the football pools, a British betting game on match results
anent is an old word meaning concerning, just as re does
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: Notes on a scheme for investing in the football pools.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former national railway; the permanent way is the track bed and rails it laid.
explanation.definitionFit: The permanent way is railway jargon for the finished track, the rails and sleepers a railway puts in place.

clue.text: Lawbreaker operating the hard way

parts.note: an echo of Proverbs 13:15, 'the way of the sinner is hard', said of anyone who breaks the law

explanation.surface: A criminal who does everything by the most difficult route.
explanation.walkthrough: The King James Bible's Proverbs says the way of the lawbreaker is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: One who breaks a law or commandment is a sinner or offender, whose path the proverb calls hard.

clue.text: Great Roman king played by Shaw

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for great, as a Roman would say it
King ... is the monarch in Shaw's play The Apple Cart

explanation.walkthrough: 'played by Shaw' means a part in a Shaw play, not an actor named Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for big gives the first sense; the second is the role of the ruler in George Bernard Shaw's political comedy The Apple Cart.

clue.text: Subjugated E European in terrible need

indicators.note: in places the East European among the jumbled letters
something terrible is a mess, so the letters of need are jumbled

parts.note: a Slav is a member of an East European people

explanation.surface: An East European finds himself in desperate want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SLAV inside ENED, the jumble of NEED made by 'terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enslaved is to be brought under complete control, the same as being subjugated.

clue.text: Hills ideal for stargazers ?

parts.note: the hills are the Los Angeles district famous as home of film stars, so fans gazing at celebrities head there, not astronomers

explanation.surface: A spot in the hills suited to astronomers with telescopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the first word of the Californian district whose second word is the clue's 'Hills'; the stars are film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Los Angeles enclave named with this word is where Hollywood stars live, so star-spotters gather there.

clue.text: If he's the one who damaged the clothes, he's a monster

parts.note: an old inverted conditional: be he means if he is

parts.words: the one who damaged the clothes
parts.note: the clothes moth's larvae eat woollens

explanation.surface: Whoever ruined the clothes must be a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: Archaic grammar turns 'if he is' into 'be he', so 'be he moth' says if he's the clothes-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is the huge beast of the Book of Job, hence any enormous monster.

clue.text: Scotsman shortly on the blower

parts.note: mon is the Scots pronunciation of man, a crossword way to call a Scotsman
soon means shortly, in a little while

explanation.surface: A Scot will be on the telephone in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blower' is British slang for the telephone, but here a blower is a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsoon is a seasonal wind of South Asia, so a mighty blower.

clue.text: Beat hollow though not in form

parts.note: someone not at home is out
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Winning easily despite playing below par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in form' looks like poor play; here OUT is not in and CLASS is a form, as a British school year group is called.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass is to be so superior as to beat a rival easily, which is to beat hollow.

clue.text: Decoration torn to bits — nasty, mean intruder !

indicators.note: an intruder breaks in, so one jumble goes inside the other
something torn to bits is broken up, so the letters of torn are rearranged
nasty here signals the letters of mean are made a mess of

explanation.surface: A treasured ornament wrecked by a vicious burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bits' gives ORNT from TORN; 'nasty' gives AMEN from MEAN, which 'intruder' puts inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is an object or feature added for decoration.

clue.text: He appears less than sharp-witted

parts.note: an old word for a simpleton, and in music the sign that lowers a sharp back to its plain note

explanation.surface: A man who seems rather slow.
explanation.walkthrough: In music a natural sign cancels a sharp, so it is lower; an old sense of the noun was a half-wit or born fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically a born fool, and in notation a note neither sharp nor flat, below a sharp.

clue.text: High range gives him a better sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a better is one who bets, and a layer is a bookmaker who lays the odds, so him a layer

explanation.surface: A mountain trip makes a man sound like a better gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: A layer is a bookie (one who lays bets); said in a British accent 'him a layer' sounds like the mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalaya is the world's highest mountain range, running across Nepal and Tibet.

clue.text: Article on Swift perhaps with long-range features

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Jonathan Swift was Dean of St Patrick's, Dublin, so an example of a dean

explanation.surface: An essay about the satirist Swift showing his far-reaching ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Long-range features are mountain ranges: Andean describes the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means of the Andes, the South American mountain chain, so marked by long ranges.

clue.text: Did this old woman find dressing exhausting ?

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for attiring, putting on clothes

explanation.surface: An elderly lady wonders whether getting dressed wore her out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this old woman' is a tiring-woman, an old name for a lady's maid who dressed her mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic sense comes from attire, clothing someone; the everyday sense is wearying.

clue.text: Risky stimulants at tennis match

definitions.meaning: large measures of different spirits drunk together, a dangerous combination
a doubles game with a man and a woman on each side

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests doping at a tennis match; read apart, a double of whisky after a double of gin is risky drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubles of assorted spirits make a dangerous drinking mix, and the same phrase names men's-and-women's pairs at tennis.

clue.text: Sussex Masquers take part in festival

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An amateur drama group from Sussex performs at a seasonal celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas, abbreviated, is the Christian festival of the Nativity.

clue.text: She would get rid of the outhouse

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as trees drop leaves
a small hut in the garden

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together: the contraction (with apostrophe), the verb and the garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction of she would, a verb for casting off, and a garden hut all share the spelling.

clue.text: Stray girl from Italy at the Opera

definitions.text: Stray girl from Italy at the Opera

parts.words: Stray girl from Italy at the Opera
parts.note: the Verdi opera's Italian title means the woman who has gone astray, a fallen woman

explanation.surface: A wandering Italian girl turns up at the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdi's opera La Traviata takes its title from the Italian for a woman led astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Verdi's opera is Italian for a woman who has strayed, so a stray girl from Italy on stage.

clue.text: Purify syntax, say ?

parts.note: split as sin tax; lust is one of the seven deadly sins
the tax half, since a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: Someone wants to clean up sentence structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the reading of 'syntax' as 'sin tax': LUST is a sin and RATE a tax (British local rates).
explanation.definitionFit: To lustrate is to purify by ritual washing or sacrifice, from the Latin lustrum.
